annotation_description: Playing Arena of Glory on turn 1 means it enters tapped (no Mountain in play), wasting the entire first turn and missing the critical turn 1 Ragavan. Arid Mesa would fetch a Mountain untapped, enabling Ragavan on turn 1 — one of Modern's most powerful openings.

Playing Ornithopter before playing a land is a sequencing error. The player should play Sacred Foundry first (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped), then cast Shadowspear for 1 mana, then cast Ornithopter for free. This gives them a 1/3 trample lifelink Ornithopter to block Ragavan on the opponent's next attack. By casting Ornithopter first without a land, they may still be able to play the land and Shadowspear afterward, but the correct sequencing principle is always land before spells to maximize options. More importantly, leading with Ornithopter before seeing if they can deploy Shadowspear in the same turn risks suboptimal ordering if any decisions branch differently.

Casting a second Ragavan (legendary, so one must be sacrificed due to the legend rule) before combat is suboptimal. The player already has a Ragavan on the battlefield, so playing another Ragavan will force them to sacrifice one due to the legend rule, wasting a card. Even if they wanted a fresh untapped Ragavan, they could have used Dash to avoid losing a card permanently. Additionally, Guide of Souls would be a better play here as it provides energy and life gain triggers when other creatures enter, and doesn't conflict with the legend rule.

message: You may choose an alternative cost
annotation_description: Ragavan is legendary. Casting a second Ragavan without Dash means one must be sacrificed to the legend rule permanently, losing a card. With Dash, they could sacrifice the existing Ragavan, attack with the hasty Dash copy (potentially getting a Treasure and card exile), and then it returns to hand at end of turn - preserving the card.

message: You may choose an alternative cost
annotation_description: Cast a second legendary Ragavan without Dash while one was already on the battlefield. The legend rule forces sacrificing one, and the new Ragavan without Dash has summoning sickness (unless Arena of Glory is exerted). Using Dash would inherently give haste and return it to hand, preserving the card for future use. Hard-casting it just wastes the card - the old Ragavan dies to legend rule and the new one is functionally equivalent or worse.

Casting Guide of Souls before combat is suboptimal when Ragavan is attacking. If Guide of Souls were cast after combat (post-Ragavan hit), the player would still have mana available and could potentially use the Ragavan trigger first. More importantly, casting a creature before combat reveals information to the opponent before they need to make blocking decisions. Additionally, the player should consider activating Arid Mesa first to fetch a land, ensuring they have the right mana available and thinning their deck. Specifically, fetching before casting ensures you don't miss a land drop if you need specific colors for Seasoned Pyromancer next turn.

Opponent has no creatures on the battlefield, so attacking with both Ragavan and Guide of Souls is risk-free. Guide of Souls attacking also triggers its attack ability (pay 3 energy for +1/+1 counters and flying on an attacker). Not attacking with Guide means missing 1 free damage and potentially the energy trigger.

Playing Colossus Hammer before playing Sunbaked Canyon is a sequencing error. The player should play their land drop first to have more mana available. With Sunbaked Canyon played first, they'd have access to more mana this turn. More importantly, playing the land first ensures they don't miss their land drop if something unexpected happens. Additionally, with Sacred Foundry, Mox Opal, and Sunbaked Canyon, they could potentially play Puresteel Paladin (WW) this turn, which would trigger a card draw from Colossus Hammer entering if they sequence correctly - play land, play Puresteel Paladin (using Sacred Foundry + Sunbaked Canyon for WW), then play Colossus Hammer to draw a card. With Puresteel Paladin on board and 3 artifacts (Mox Opal, Shadowspear, Colossus Hammer), they'd have Metalcraft for equip 0, enabling a powerful setup.

Casting Seasoned Pyromancer before activating Arid Mesa means the 2 cards drawn from Pyromancer's ETB come from a slightly thicker deck. Fetching first would thin the deck before the draws, marginally improving card quality. Additionally, having the extra land on board before committing mana is better sequencing practice.

message: Select a Mountain or Plains card
annotation_description: MiMo Spike fetched a basic Mountain when they already have abundant red mana (Sacred Foundry + 2 Arena of Glory + Treasure Token) and only one white source (Sacred Foundry). Their Boros deck runs cards like Puresteel Paladin (WW), Stoneforge Mystic (1W), and Battlefield Improvisation (1W) that need white mana.

Puresteel Paladin with Metalcraft already active (3 artifacts: Mox Opal, Shadowspear, Colossus Hammer) would enable equipping Colossus Hammer for {0}, the deck's primary game plan. Stoneforge Mystic searches for more equipment when the hand/board is already loaded with equipment.

message: When <font color='#F0E68C' object_id='d5e8ae45-c24f-4972-abb9-3b3e3349d08d'>Stoneforge Mystic</font> [d5e] enters, you may search your library for an Equipment card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle.
annotation_description: Searched for Leyline Axe when they already had one in hand. Paradise Mantle (0-cost equipment) was available and would have been much better - it's free to cast, triggers Puresteel Paladin draws, contributes to Metalcraft, and provides mana. The existing Leyline Axe in hand can be cheated into play via Stoneforge Mystic's activated ability.

At 5 life facing 5 total damage from three attackers (Ragavan 2/1, Guide of Souls ~1/1, Seasoned Pyromancer 2/2) with Goblin Bombardment on the opponent's side, only blocking with one creature leaves more unblocked damage than necessary. Blocking with both Stoneforge Mystic and Puresteel Paladin on two different attackers would prevent more damage and improve survival chances.
